items.title: Joe Wilder Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 12, 1998
items.q: I asked him about it and he said, “well you’d better speak to Gladys” his wife. ... So I spoke to her and she said, “yes what is it, young man?”

ctx.x: Yeah. You had a lot of that. And you would go work in clubs and things and they would pay the guys a pittance. They were making good money but they wouldn’t give it to them. Well Lionel Hampton was a good case in point. I joined that band and I was making eleven dollars a night, and I was playing, at that time, the first trumpet part. I wasn’t playing the high things, he had guys there, Ernie Royal and guys who did that. But I was supposed to be the first trumpet player and I was getting eleven dollars a night,…

“hey” — if you will excuse the language — “who in the hell do you think you are?” This was exactly the way he asked me. And I looked at him and I said, “who in the hell do you think YOU are?” And I turned around and walked out and that night I told Lionel, I said, “if I don’t get fifteen dollars a night from tonight on, I’m out, you’ll have to get somebody else.” And so he said, “well I’ll talk to Gladys about it.” So he spoke to her and as of the next night they did pay me fifteen dollars a night. But that was…
